summary: Ingested 2026-10-29-survival-and-monetization.md: 20 hypotheses (7 tested and 1 qualitative on Most Popular, 8 tested and 3 qualitative on Top Earning, 1 cross-chart qualitative).

The research says cheap repeatable 9-49 R$ products drive spending, while H-te-005 consistently finds a median product price above 79 R$ goes with higher efficiency; both are kept, and the new prod_skip test will help separate having a cheap product from pricing most products high.

The research says skill-light loops earn the most per player-hour, while combat PvP loops consistently earn higher Top Earning positions (H-te-022); the new competitive_core test on te_eff will show which holds in tracked games.
The research's rolls-and-eggs advice also sits against H-te-002 (pet and egg games consistently earn less per CCU); both are kept.
Survival framing lifts breakout charts (Up-and-Coming, Top Trending) yet consistently earns less per player on Top Earning, the same reach-versus-revenue split as the steal/egg template (H-x-002).
Halloween events lift old horror and anomaly games across charts this week, a seasonal confounder for update, event and age hypotheses.
progressions: uc→tt remains the most common transition (135 entries, median 2 days), ahead of tt→mp (114, 2 days).
uc→te (83, 5 days), tt→te (80, 4 days), te→tt (74, 9 days) and uc→mp (72, 4 days) show breakouts reaching revenue and dominance within about a week, while tt→uc stays at 1.
